mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent corporate revenue reductions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% in one month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which typically reduces borrowing costs and increases liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with subsequent easing cycles.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of UNRATE and PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% YoY, it signals a weakening demand coupled with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and CPIAUCSL increases > 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of HOUST and CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent stagflationary pressures.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, when the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising, it signals tightening supply conditions and monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of INDPRO and FEDFUNDS does not correlate with subsequent tightening conditions.
